summary: Richard von Garbe worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Marienstiftsgymnasium, the University of Tübingen (PhD 1873-1877) under Rudolf von Roth and Hermann Grassmann, and Königsberg. He held posts at Königsberg (1878-1895) and Tübingen (1895-1927).

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.

Rico Sennrich specializes in computational linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Zurich (2004-2013), where he held a post around 2011, and later served as a lecturer at the University of Edinburgh from 2015 to 2022.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Rigzin Lhundup worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1959 and 1987.

Riika J. Virtanen works in the field of Tibetology. She completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rik Pinxten is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He earned two doctorates at Ghent University in 1975 and served on the faculty there from 1981 to 2012.

Rikizan Ishikawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1971. He served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at Komazawa University from around 1985 to 1997.

Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Tubten Tsondru.

Rinzin Thargyal worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oslo, completing his Magister degree by 1985 under the supervision of Fredrik Barth and temporary supervisor Arne Martin Klausen.
Rita Gupta is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied under David Friedman and held a post at North-Eastern Hill University.

Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004), later holding posts at the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UW–Milwaukee and the University of Chicago under Eliade, Long, and Kitagawa. She held posts at UW–Eau Claire (1973–1998) and UW–Madison (attested 1990).

Rizong Sras Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, training at Drepung Loseling Monastery under the 14th Dalai Lama, Losal Ling Khen Zur Jampal Sampel, and Pema Gyaltsen. He was Abbot of Gyume, Samstanling, and Drepung Loseling, and 102nd Ganden Tripa.

Ričardas Mironas specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Vytautas Magnus University (~1928-1933) and the Sorbonne (~1933-1936), later teaching at Vytautas Magnus University (1944, 1946) and serving as professor at Vilnius University from 1950.

Rob Linrothe works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and art history. He studied at Minnesota, the Inter-University Program, and Chicago (PhD ~1992). He held posts at the National Palace Museum, Skidmore College (1992-2009), Rubin Museum, and Northwestern University (2010-2022).

Rob Nairn was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, and the University of Edinburgh. He held academic posts in law and criminology at the University of Zimbabwe and the University of Cape Town.

Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Geshe Wangyal, Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He held posts at Amherst College (1973-1988) and Columbia University (1988-2019).

Robert A. Hall, Jr. was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Sapienza University of Rome, and Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield and Carl Darling Buck. He taught at Puerto Rico, Princeton, and Brown, and was professor at Cornell from 1946 to 1976.

Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin, earning his PhD by 2002 under Patrick Olivelle, and held a post there attested in 1996.
